findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects stored in it are not encrypted at rest by default.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated with this bucket, so it can be made public via ACL or policy changes without any account-level guardrail.
This bucket stores ledger/financial export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined for this bucket, leaving it without protection against accidental public exposure.
The bucket has versioning and logging configured but lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined for this bucket to prevent it from becoming publicly accessible.
This bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbook data is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined for this bucket, leaving it without protection against accidental public exposure.

Although this bucket uses KMS encryption, there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so account/bucket-level guardrails against public exposure are absent despite the log-delivery-write ACL.
